chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, that he said: We were told by Muhammad bin Ahmad, from Musa bin Umar, from Muhammad bin Isma'il bin Bazee', from Ibrahim bin Mahzam, from the one he narrates from, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If you enter Mecca, then buy dates with a dirham and give it as charity due to what came from you during your state of Ihram for the Umrah. Then, when you are finished with your pilgrimage, then buy dates with a dirham and give it as charity. Then, if you enter Medina, do the same as that.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: State of ritual consecration for pilgrimage or minor pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended charity to give when entering Mecca and Medina for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar* outlines a specific ritual of expiation (kaffarah) for minor deficiencies in the Ihram state, prescribing the donation of dates purchased with a dirham at three pivotal moments: entering Mecca, post-Hajj, and entering Medina. Scholarly tradition interprets this as a means to purify the pilgrimage rites and maintain spiritual humility, linking material charity directly to the validity and perfection of the Umrah and Hajj obligations.

en.basel-kadem: 9.	We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Ahmad, from Musa bin Umar, from Muhammed bin Isma’eel bin Bazee’, from Ibrahim bin Mahzam, from the one he narrates from, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

If you enter Mecca, then buy dates with a dirham and give it as charity due to what came from you during your state of Ihram for the Umrah. Then, when you are finished with your pilgrimage, then buy dates with a dirham and give it as charity. Then, if you enter Medina, do the same as that.
